Exercise coaching boosts colon cancer survival

📅 06 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1034 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.
  • According to recent reports, the question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care.
  • Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In 2025, an international trial found that people treated for colon cancer were more likely to be alive eight years later if they had received long-term exercise coaching.

According to recent reports, the question facing doctors now is less whether people with cancer should exercise, and rather how they should build it into routine care. In the US, that shift is reaching hospital standards. From January 2027, breast cancer centers must screen patients' physical function and recommend exercise or physical therapy where needed.

Yet experts caution that the trial's findings may not apply to every cancer or every patient.

It has been revealed that the 2025 trial, called CHALLENGE, was led by the Canadian Cancer Trials Group. It began enrolling patients in 2009 and published its results in 2025.

It has been revealed that the trial's 889 participants came from six countries, most from Canada and Australia. All had finished surgery and chemotherapy for stage 2 or 3 colon cancer, which had not spread to distant organs.

It has been revealed that half received only health education materials on exercise and healthy eating. The other half additionally met a physical activity consultant for three years.

According to recent reports, in the exercise group, the target was similar to adding 45 to 60 minutes of brisk walking, three to four times a week. The amount and type of activity varied from person to person, noted Tormod Skogstad Nilsen, a cancer exercise researcher in Norway. But he said participants achieved lasting increases in their physical activity.

Exercise helped. People in the exercise group were less likely to see their cancer come back, to develop a latest cancer or to die. In all, 93 had at least one of these setbacks, compared with 131 in the health education group.

Sources indicate that in cancer research, living longer usually means a larger share of people is still alive at a given point. It does not promise anyone a set number of extra years.

Industry observers note that eight years after joining CHALLENGE, about 90 of every 100 people in the exercise group were alive, compared with about 83 of every 100 in the health education group. That is about 7% more people alive in the group who had guided exercise.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that for people without cancer, the evidence comes from studies that follow people's habits and health over many years. These can show a link, but not prove cause and effect. Active people may also eat better or smoke less.

In another 2025 study, more than 85,000 adults in the United Kingdom wore a wrist tracker for a week. Over about six years, those who moved most had a 26% lower risk of 13 cancers, including breast and colorectal cancer, than those who moved least.

Even light activity, such as household chores, was linked to lower risk. The link held after researchers accounted for lifestyle, weight and other health conditions.

Earlier research, based on people's self-reporting, has led to similar conclusions. A 2016 analysis of 1.44 million adults in the US and Europe linked free-time activity to a lower risk of many cancers, largely regardless of weight or smoking.

A trial to prove prevention is unlikely: Many cancers take years to develop, so it would need huge numbers of people followed for a long time.

CHALLENGE included only people with colon cancer. But how it picked participants offers a clue: Before joining, they had to pass a fitness test.

Anna Campbell, a professor of clinical exercise science at Edinburgh Napier University in Scotland, sees that as a guide.

"I think patients with any other cancer stage II and III who have a reasonable baseline level of fitness and no major comorbidities that would prevent them from undertaking moderate to vigorous activity could be considered for similar interventions," she said. Comorbidities are other health conditions.

Nilsen noted some people decline to join exercise trials because they feel too unwell or tired, or do not want to exercise. "Hence, study populations are typically younger, 'healthier', and most times slightly more motivated compared to a clinical population," he said.

The coaching aimed to make activity a lasting habit, and Campbell said that is where the trial's value lies.

"The main success of the study is that it enabled the participants to become independent exercisers staying active in a safe and effective and individualized way," she noted.

In a recent development, nilsen agreed. Helping people become more active "in their own environment," without depending on a well-equipped training center, "would likely lead to more sustainable activity behavioral changes," he said.

Industry observers note that he is wary of fixed targets, however. "Exercise should be tailored to each individual and the challenges they face, rather than striving to reach a given minimum of exercise required," though health care resources may not always allow it, he added.

It has been revealed that in a 2024 survey of 549 people with cancer, only one in 10 had been referred to an exercise service. Yet almost three in four thought their oncologist should raise the subject.

Sources indicate that "There are some excellent examples of effective pathways but these are few and far between," said Campbell. Good services bring everyone on board, from surgeons to community fitness instructors.

"Ideally, one person in the clinical setting needs to champion the program to link all the team together.".

Campbell expects CHALLENGE's regular coaching will be cut back in everyday care. Apps and live online group sessions could still work, she noted, if run by properly trained staff.

One recent study of live online exercise engaged patients from poorer backgrounds, in rural areas and with advanced cancer. "It answered some of the barriers, such as cost, travel and lack of confidence," she stated.

Patients can ask their care team what exercise is safe for them and what support exists.

According to recent reports, according to Nilsen, a training session can bring structure and manufacturer. "You made it here, despite your feeling unwell or fatigued this morning, so you feel mastery based on that," he remarked.

  • Sources indicate that artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that homo erectus might have also lived in rainforests — previously thought to be a habitat in which only modern humans could have thrived.Credit: S. Entressangle/E. Daynes/SPL.

Fossil teeth suggest that Homo erectus thrived in dense rainforests in southern China as recently as 180,000 years ago. Researchers had thought that these ancient hominins had been limited to savannahs and open woodlands, indicates Kira Westaway, a geochronologist and a co-author of two new studies. “This is a really major deal, because we thought Homo sapiens were the only species that had the skill set to survive in really challenging rainforest environments.”.

Reference: Nature paper 1 & paper 2.

Sources indicate that artificial-intelligence giant Anthropic has made history with the largest initial public offering (IPO) on record on 19 November. The firm — now valued at a staggering US$1.5 trillion — has major ambitions in science. It made waves earlier this year when it reported that its model Claude had made several major mathematics breakthroughs. The organization also launched their first ‘wet’ laboratory for life sciences research and has announced looks to “substantially” scale up its work in AI-enabled drug discovery. Pitched as a company that prioritizes AI safety, some researchers question whether an IPO — and the accompanying investor demands — might disrupt some of Anthropic’s safety commitments.

Roughly 180 million people could be carrying a previously unknown type of giant virus in their guts. Researchers found DNA from these ‘egoviruses’ in gut samples from people, buffalo, goats, chickens, deer and pigs. Six clades were unique to people, one of which is estimated to be present in roughly 1% of the population. Microbiologists say that egoviruses could be the missing link between giant viruses that infect single-celled organisms and distantly related poxviruses, such as those that cause smallpox and mpox, which can infect people and animals directly.

Here in Washington DC, tens of thousands of researchers have gathered for the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting — a showcase for everything from neural implants to memory research.

But when I asked a panel of leaders at the US National Institutes of Health what in neuroscience remains underappreciated, several pointed to the brain’s relationship with the rest of the body. Nora Volkow, director of the National Institute on Drug Abuse, lamented the lack of research into brain metabolism — a blind spot exposed by the surprising neurological effects of GLP-1 drugs.

It has been revealed that amy Bany Adams, acting director of the National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, offered a reminder of how much remains to be discovered. Of the glymphatic system, the brain’s waste-clearance network, she mentioned: “We didn’t even know it existed when I was in graduate school.” I’m leaving with a longer list of questions about what else we’ve been overlooking.

According to recent reports, neuroscientists are uncovering how the brain orchestrates a tailored mixture of symptoms in response to either a bacterial or viral infection. Presenting at the Society for Neuroscience’s annual meeting on 15 November, researchers suggested that the brain decodes the type of pathogen that has invaded, accesses memories of past bouts of illness and can even mobilize immune defences at the sight of a sick person. The unpublished findings challenge the long-held view that neurological responses to infection are a one-size-fits-all response to inflammation.

Sources indicate that artificial-intelligence governance requires more than companies’ oversight of their models — it requires “a system of accountability” that works like a national constitution, argues legal scholar Cindy Skach. Firms should be held legally liable when individuals are affected by AI actions that infringe on their fundamental rights, Skach suggests. She proposes ‘human dignity’ as the most important value for the system to uphold. When a person’s dignity is violated — by an AI-generated deepfake or by a chatbot that treats a distressed user as just another interaction — they could petition a court directly to hold the perpetrator accountable.

Do you find networking a nightmare? Three experts share — in the form of short videos — how to grasp the nettle. They suggest thinking about networking as a professional skill that can be learnt and developed, considering arriving early for events and not worrying about volume. One high-quality connection and follow-up conversation is worth more than 100 business cards, says public-speaking coach Susie Ashfield.

Recent findings suggest that in the second episode of Nature Podcast’s climate miniseries, host Nick Petrić Howe hears from scientists about what humanity can actually do to stop the runaway train of rising temperatures. The rise of renewable-energy technologies is already making a dent in greenhouse-gas emissions, experts say. But creating meat alternatives and a move away from an economic system that incentivizes ‘growth at any cost’ could help to really shift the dial.

Nature Podcast | 45 min listen or read the transcript.

In a recent development, vertebrate palaeontologist Aldo Benites-Palomino explains why the extinct ancient whale — which evolved extreme facial asymmetry to to make space in its head for echolocation and sound production organs — was named with a Peruvian word for “anything that is flashy, over-the-top, bizarre, extravagant or difficult to categorize aesthetically”. (Discover | 7 min read).

Reference: Communications Biology paper.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03797-3.

Today I’m considering buying a prickly pear cactus (Opuntia) in case of a power cut. Researchers have found that the plants’ unusual method of photosynthesis can be harnessed to generate a small amount of electricity, with around eight prickly pears together generating nearly three times the voltage of a standard AA battery.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a new manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 14:40 EST, 20 November 2026.

In a recent development, diet Pep is losing his fizz. Enzo Maresca may look like Pep Guardiola, may have learned his craft under his Manchester City predecessor, but his quest to follow in his mentor’s footsteps has all gone a bit flat.

Seven successive Premier League wins to start his City reign, a record for a new manager in the competition, breaking one jointly-held by Guardiola, gave the impression that this might be a smooth passing of the torch after all.

Three months in, and three defeats on the spin that left them six points behind Arsenal have made it clear that something is not clicking for Maresca.

According to recent reports, is the uncertainty around the potential punishment following that guilty verdict taking its toll? Is Maresca just suffering from his usual late autumn dips? He suffered similar tricky periods around late October and early November at Leicester and his first season at Chelsea too.

Or is there something at the heart of his side, of his system, that’s finally being exposed?

Enzo Maresca's Man City have slumped to three straight Premier League defeats after a promising start to the season.

According to recent reports, guardiola’s City was all about control. Keep the ball, dominate the pitch, play the game at your pace, on your terms.

Maresca’s City, regardless of how well they started the season, has been about anything but. It has been about triumph amid chaos, about moments of magic more than the overarching method.

Without that control, City’s defensive challenges have been laid bare. The 13 goals they have let in after 10 games is their most at this stage since 2008. They haven’t kept a clean sheet in their last eight matches in all competitions. That's a drought longer than at any point under Guardiola.

Their biggest problem over City's three successive Premier League defeats is just how susceptible they have been to counter attacks.

Only Newcastle have faced more shots this season following ‘fast breaks’ – data giants Opta's term for counter attacks – than City’s 17, and 11 of those have come in the last three games: six against Nottingham Forest, two of which led to goals, three against Brighton and another two against Aston Villa.

According to recent reports, maresca’s side are being more profligate in possession, too. Over the first seven games of the season, they lost the ball 120 times a game on average – one of the best figures in the division. Since then, it’s closer to 140.

City have been wasteful in possession and regularly overrun on the counter, with Elliot Anderson (centre) too often left isolated in midfield.

ANDERSON CAN'T DO IT ALL ON HIS OWN.

Industry observers note that many of these problems have their roots in Maresca's serious problems in midfield. Rodri, the best holding midfielder of his generation, was always going to be hard to replace but Maresca appears to be expecting Elliot Anderson to do it all on his own.

Industry observers note that anderson is at his best when he’s free to get up and down the pitch, box to box, using his physicality not just in winning the ball back but progressing it. No midfielder played more passes into the final third last season than Anderson at Forest. At one stage of the campaign, he had played more progressive passes than any other player across Europe’s top five leagues.

And yet Maresca is forcing Anderson to play as the sitter while his golden boy Enzo Fernandez, whom he pushed City to sign in the summer for £125million, is roaming free and high up the pitch.

Maresca likes his teams to build up in a 3-1-6 shape, which sees Fernandez push up as an extra attacking midfielder, and leaves Anderson manning the fort alone.

When City lose the ball, though, it leaves them wide open.

Sources indicate that this is the opening goal City conceded against Forest. Josko Gvardiol wants to play the ball inside but has only red shirts and empty green space ahead of him. Anderson is the only man free, but even he is too high and has a Forest player ready to cut off the pass. Eventually, Gvardiol gets robbed and Forest score.

Recent findings suggest that A lack of options for Josko Gvardiol (left) led to Forest's opener against City. Enzo Fernandez (circled) was caught high up the pitch, way ahead of the deeper Anderson (also circled).

Here’s another moment in the defeat by Brighton.

Industry observers note that the Seagulls break forward on the flank and Anderson races over to close the ball down. Fernandez is, you guessed it, high up the pitch.

City have no midfield cover to stop the ball inside, Abdukodir Khusanov gets drawn in and leaves loads of space in behind for Yasin Ayari to exploit and cross to Maxim De Cuyper for a great chance.

The lack of protection offered by Anderson and especially the more advanced Fernandez was again on show against Brighton, who were able to exploit the acres of space left in midfield.

Fernandez is doing what Maresca wants, but it’s not working. Maresca needs more from him, especially when Anderson’s instincts are to press and harass and bully, which can leave gaps when he does not yet read the game as comprehensively as Rodri.

Recent findings suggest that anderson sits in the top five for ball recoveries among midfielders to have played 500 minutes this season. Fernandez is in the bottom five. That figure becomes even more alarming when you consider Anderson has created more chances from open play than Fernandez, too.

Ayyoub Bouaddi demonstrated at the World Cup that he had the most similar profile to Rodri. It might be time for Maresca to put some faith in him.

Maresca has always wanted his goalkeeper to be an 11th outfielder. In his one season at Leicester, Mads Hermansen played more passes than any goalkeeper in Championship history. During his time at Chelsea, there was a shaky moment in a draw with Arsenal when loud groans greeted a misplaced pass from Robert Sanchez.

‘I am the guy who asks Robert to do that,’ remarked Maresca after that game. ‘The moment he stops doing that, he is not going to play.’.

According to recent reports, donnarumma, though, for all his (usually) excellent shot-stopping, is anything but a ball-playing goalkeeper. The ball rolled under his foot from a simple back pass against Coventry and so nearly crept over the line. He gifted France an early lead while on international duty with Italy when he passed the ball straight to Michael Olise.

Only two keepers made more errors leading to shots than Donnarumma across the course of last season, with many of those being with his feet, like when he gifted Kai Havertz an equaliser in City's victory over Arsenal in April.

Gianluigi Donnarumma has never been good with his feet - now his excellent shot-stopping has taken a dip too.

The Italian should have easily dealt with Nicolas Jackson's second goal in City's 2-1 loss at Aston Villa.

The decision to let James Trafford leave in the summer, especially with Guardiola’s impending departure and a manager like Maresca coming in, is looking ever more misguided.

Trafford is not immune to mistakes either, of course. He erred badly when trying to play out from the back for City against Spurs last season and made an almost identical howler for Leeds at Bournemouth in October. But he is still far more confident at playing out from the back than Donnarumma.

The double blow for Maresca is that the trade-off with Donnarumma – where he makes up for his weakness with the ball at his feet by making saves that other keepers can’t make – is no longer paying off either.

Nicolas Jackson’s shot squirmed straight through him to hand Villa victory and condemn City to their first defeat of the season.

When you are coughing up chances as frequently as City are, Maresca needs his keeper to be on top form.

According to recent reports, do you know who is keeping the ball out of his net? James Trafford. He boasts the highest save percentage of any goalkeeper in the top flight, keeping out 81 per cent of the shots on target coming his way. Donnarumma is 15th, on less than 66 per cent.

It has been revealed that according to Opta’s expected data, Trafford has also prevented more than four goals that he should have conceded from the quality of the shots he’s faced. Again, he’s the best in the Premier League. Donnarumma is middle of the pack.

‘At the moment, I’m not thinking about the goalkeeping situation,’ remarked Maresca recently. Without Trafford there and just 34-year-old Geronimo Rulli as back-up, he doesn’t really have a choice but to persist with Donnarumma and hope he improves.

When the goals stop flowing for Erling Haaland, City can't mask all their other problems.

So used are we now to seeing the Norwegian on the scoresheet, having notched nine in City’s opening eight matches, that when he goes just two games without a goal it feels as if he’s on a barren spell.

The concern, though, is less down to Haaland and more that City’s build-up in recent weeks is struggling to get him into the game.

Sources indicate that city are finding it more difficult to get Haaland on the ball. His touches per game are falling steadily but, crucially, so are the quality of the chances his team-mates are creating for him.

Industry observers note that haaland had more than one Opta-defined 'substantial chance' in five of City’s opening seven games. He’s had just one come his way in each of their three defeats.

According to recent reports, his expected goals (xG) tally is dropping too. Across City’s winning streak, Haaland’s average xG per match was 0.81. Only once, against Liverpool, did it drop below 0.5.

Over the three defeats, it’s just 0.45 and has not once gone above 0.5.

Antoine Semenyo missing the last three games through injury has not helped, especially when teams now try to pack the middle of the pitch and force City wide.

Haaland will come good, he always does, but City need to start serving him again if Maresca wants to get through this tricky spell and stop the vultures from circling.

It has been revealed that it's time for some brackets as the MLS Cup playoffs are upon us. With the Wild Card round kicking off on Thursday night, 18 teams (still too many) will enter the gauntlet that is the playoffs. All eyes will be on Nashville SC, who have a first-round bye after winning the Supporters' Shield and setting a new MLS regular-season points record with 77 points. However, when it comes down to it, anyone can fall in a one-off match, as being successful in the regular season is a different proposition than doing so in the postseason.

According to recent reports, while the Wild Card round is a one-off, win-or-go-home match, the first round is a best-of-three series with games going to a penalty shootout if tied. That can change the calculus a bit, especially for teams getting an early goal in the first game, since there are still two more chances to advance. But since there are playoffs, that also means that we have to predict the bracket, so let's get to it.

According to recent reports, the Seattle Sounders come into this postseason in a tough spot. While they've become a team that can't be counted out of MLS Cup contention, they enter the playoffs without one of their best defenders. Center back Jackson Ragen was suspended for two games following a disciplinary review for his challenge on Los Angeles FC's Jacob Shaffelburg. While the Sounders have returned to health, this opens the door for Real Salt Lake to get out of the Wild Card round.

According to recent reports, in Orlando, this is one of the matchups of the entire playoffs as Evander and Antoine Griezmann will battle in a match where defense is optional. Both teams had higher ambitions heading into the season, so for the loser, it could have major implications. But after winning Newcomer of the Year, Griezmann, alongside Orlando's strong attack, will prove to be too much to handle for Cincinnati as we head to the first round of the playoffs proper.

Industry observers note that the parity in MLS this season, especially in the Western Conference, is real. You could tell me that anyone would come out of the West, and it's believable. Vancouver may be the team to beat, but needing to replace Sebastian Berhalter and Andres Cubas midseason did hurt the squad. Jesper Sorensen has done plenty to keep Vancouver afloat, but they're still vulnerable, although that'll be more of an issue in later rounds depending on how the bracket shakes out. St. Louis City SC have already exceeded expectations by winning the U.S. Open Cup, and if Alexandru Matan is on his game, they may be unbeatable, but they can run hot and cold. Add in Bruce Arena still evolving with the league and the cardiac kids of Dallas (and of course the brilliance of Petar Musa), and that brings us to the advancing sides. I would apologize to Los Angeles FC, but post-Steve Cherundolo, this is a side that has faltered, and a long look needs to be taken at the squad following the season to move forward.

Recent findings suggest that in the East, we're in B.J. Callaghan's world. Los Angeles FC are the last team to do the double of winning the Supporters' Shield and MLS Cup, and it's a tough thing for Nashville to do, but this team has only allowed 25 goals in a full season. They can score, they can grind a game to a halt, and they have so many ways to give the opposition fits. In a best-of-three, good luck getting past them. Speaking of slowing a game down, the New England Revolution are a worst-case matchup for the fighting Cavan Sullivans of Philadelphia. Joshua Wynder has stabilized the defense in front of Matt Turner, and while the Revolution may not have a high ceiling as constructed, the floor is so high in this unique setup. Charlotte facing Chicago might as well be a coin flip. Then there's Miami facing Columbus. Like the Union, the Crew can win because their attacking upside is so high, and Miami are a flawed team, but Lionel Messi is still doing Lionel Messi things. San Jose's run comes to an end here, while St. Louis and Dallas fight in an evenly matched clash to determine who else comes out of the Western Conference. Nashville's defense again puts up a suffocating performance to get past Charlotte, and Messi drives Inter Miami past the Revolution, setting up a fascinating set of conference finals.

According to recent reports, okay, I swear that this wasn't supposed to go chalk with three of the top four finishers in the regular season making it to the conference finals, but getting to the end of the season and saying that the good teams are actually good shouldn't be revolutionary. Thomas Muller and Brian White are enough to push the Whitecaps to the MLS Cup final, where the Eastern Conference yet again comes down to Messi versus Hany Mukhtar. Nashville may be the better-coached team, but Miami have found a way with their backs against the wall to produce a rematch of last season's MLS Cup final.

Muller and Messi have faced each other 11 times, with Muller claiming seven wins to Messi's four. However, after getting one over on Muller last season, Messi isn't going to let a chance at a second consecutive MLS Cup pass by, even if this one is in Vancouver amid the uncertain future of BC Place as the home of the Whitecaps.

  • At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.
  • Industry observers note that roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

Industry observers note that roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

And then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

It has been revealed that united fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

And yet by the 86th minute Matheus Cunha’s wild celebrations were encapsulating a wild night, the Brazilian ripping off his shirt after his dramatic winner before launching himself into a delirious crowd drunk on the euphoria of a victory that had seemed improbable in the extreme at the interval, when boos cascaded from the stands.

Sources indicate that whether this proves little more than a thrilling, heroic interlude in the endgame for Carrick, or the start of a genuine turnaround, is hard to know. And, let’s be clear, there was so much about the first-half performance to concern the hierarchy, who came under persistent, furious attack from fans at war with an ownership it reviles and wants gone.

But the second half stood firmly at odds with the shambolic display that had preceded it and suggested all may not be quite lost just yet.

Aston Villa visit Old Trafford on Sunday in the final game before the international break and, if Carrick can follow this with another win, then it will be intriguing to see where the Old Trafford board goes from there.

Carrick may at least have been encouraged by some of the things Bruno Fernandes said after the game, not least that he warranted being dropped against Bournemouth. And it was the captain who kick-started the fightback against Roma, albeit at the second attempt.

In a recent development, he had won the penalty after being fouled by Gianluca Mancini only to then contrive to miss it. But a retake was ordered for encroachment and, given a second bite at the cherry, Fernandes made no mistake.

NO MISTAKE THIS TIME 💪 Bruno Fernandes gets United back in it after a penalty retake 😤 https://t.co/uQdkNs0lXo.

When Carlos Baleba pulled up with a hamstring injury within seconds of the restart as he burst into the penalty area, Carrick must have wondered what else could go wrong.

But as United went hell for leather, the home supporters who had spent much of the first half attacking the owners and staging a number of colourful protest acts, suddenly found their voice in a very different way.

Recent findings suggest that from being an atmosphere in which the players clearly felt cowed, Old Trafford was now rallying behind its men in red – and it helped to shake Roma in the process. They had been such good value for their lead, but now they were rocking, and United smelled blood.

There was wave after wave of attack as Roma desperately and often frantically tried to defend their goal, and it took a bad mistake from Leonardo Balerdi, who swung at thin air from Fernandes’s cross and missed the ball, to hand Cunha the chance to equalise.

IT'S 2-2! 💥 Cunha levels it up for United! 🔴🇧🇷 https://t.co/q60oQUoat1.

At that point, the momentum was firmly in United’s favour and three minutes later they were in front. It is a source of bemusement among fans that Shea Lacey has not had more game-time considering how poor some senior players have been. And his arrival as a substitute made a big difference.

Sources indicate that it was Lacey who speared an inch-perfect pass into Cunha, who turned sharply before drilling a stunning finish in off the near post. Cue bedlam.

MAN UNITED HAVE TURNED IT AROUND!!! 🔴🔥 From 2-0 down, to 3-2 up at Old Trafford 🤩 https://t.co/ATD8wDlc1e.

Industry observers note that cunha was booked for taking off his shirt as he crowd-surfed bear-chested among the fans and was then sent off minutes later after a poor challenge. A fittingly chaotic end to a crazy night for the match-winner.

Industry observers note that the difference to those opening 45 minutes was as stark as it gets. Indeed, the first half felt like a continuation from the fans of their blood-letting against Bournemouth.

Sources indicate that when the clock hit 20.05 – a nod to the year 2005 when the Glazers bought the club – a pile of tennis balls were thrown on to the pitch from the Stretford End amid chants of “We Want Glazers Out”. They were promptly followed by cries of “Just like the Glazers, Jim Ratcliffe’s a c---” and “sell the club and f--- off home”.

Jason Wilcox, the club’s director of football, again copped for it. A banner read: “For the love, not the ‘likes’”. When the Champions League music played, hundreds of green and gold balloons – a reference to the club’s original colours and the 2010 protest movement – were released.

On the pitch, United were all over the place. Carrick had dropped Lisandro Martínez after his red card against Chelsea but his replacement Ayden Heaven was at fault for the first goal after getting sucked in and failing to check his shoulder. Had he done, he would have seen Matías Soulé unmarked and in acres of space with Diogo Dalot, United’s left-back, caught high up the pitch. Soulé made no mistake with his finish.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬 United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 https://t.co/DtIOFJYZ6D.

Heaven almost did the same again soon after before more blunders handed Roma a second. Soulé tried to find Donyell Malen with a pass but miscued to Harry Maguire. Yet the England defender then proceeded to give the ball straight back to Soulé, who turned Dalot and shot with Heaven blocking the ball with his right arm as he lunged to stop the effort. Malen continued his rich scoring vein from the penalty spot.

Malen makes it TWO-NIL ROMA from the spot, after a handball from Heaven in the box 😬 https://t.co/kUeOeQNRES.

Recent findings suggest that at that point, no one could have reckoned on the comeback that followed. Where it leads, who knows.

Speaking after the match, Michael Carrick was very positive about his side’s performance.

According to recent reports, “It was a good night. I have to a lot of credit to the players for starters, showing that character and that quality when we needed it and to the supporters. This place does incredible, magical things,” noted Carrick.

According to recent reports, “I thought we grew into it the first half  after giving the goals too easily. We spoke at half time about how this place can change, it only takes one moment and it certainly did that and the boys made the most of every opportunity and were fantastic in the end.”.

Asked about how he inspired the team at half-time he kept it simple: “Just not to get too disappointed about things. I thought we were coming into the game, getting around their box and it didn’t feel that way to the players because they were carrying too much frustration and disappointment and I knew we were doing some good things in the game against a really good team.

“Playing against man-to-man as much as they are, you probably get more failure than success and it’s still being positive and the boys responded so well to that.”.

As for whether this will change United’s momentum now, he was cautious not to get carried away.

Recent findings suggest that “Listen it’s one game. It depends on what happens next and we’ve got to capitalise on that but tonight the boys showed an awful lot,” he stated.

“And I thought we came out the second half, unfortunately with Carlos having to go off and Youri coming on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic, he highlighted everything that he is as a personality, as a character and with his experience to step in the game like that, and the boys just went with the flow and you could feel how positive it was and it was nice to see this place like that again.”.

Captain Bruno Fernandes also spoke after the match, acknowledging the difficulties the team has faced.

In a recent development, “It’s tough to say something at the moment to be honest. It’s been a tough period for us, we have not been able to play in the way we want, get the results we want. We’ve done some good bits, but not had the consistency to do it through a whole game to get results and it’s been tough.

“But today was key to get a win. We knew after that we still had the fans with us, we felt we could change it with a goal and something and fortunately we did it today.”.

As for his penalty miss and re-take: “First one didn’t go the way I wanted, I did something wrong but I got a second chance and I cleared my head and my mind was only on to get the ball in back of the net.

“It’s been tough for the fans, we understand that. Having that belief from their side helps the team a lot and today was one of those days that Old Trafford came alive.”.

After his first start as he returns from injury, Kobbie Mainoo was full of praise for the fans, saying he cherished the relationship the team had with them.

“It’s unlike anything else. We’d do anything for these fans on the pitch, all the love they give us throughout the season it’s only right we repay them and it’s a bit of fun just jumping into the stands with them.”.

Speaking to Amazon after the match, Youri Tielemans said: “There has been a lot of pressure on him [Carrick] and that’s how we repay him, with a comeback like this, major character, big fight.”.

Recent findings suggest that “We just kept working, we kept believing. We were on the front foot in the second half, we tried to push them into their goal and we succeeded.”.

As for whether or not the performance would be enough to keep Carrick in his role at United: “That’s a different question. The only thing we can do is stick behind him, fight for him and fight for the club.

“At the end of the day we are on the pitch and we need to show what we are capable of and tonight, especially in the second half, we demonstrated what we can do and we turned up the gears.

“Let’s hope this is a good turnaround for us and let’s hope we can build on this.”.

According to recent reports, “Great credit to Michael Carrick because they were down and out at half-time. They were everywhere in that first-half, and he had to change and tweak things,” Alan Shearer remarked after the final whistle.

“I stated what can he do, I didn’t know where he would start, and he must have started in the dressing room, and pointing at a few people telling them to be brave and courageous and move the ball quicker, and run in behind and they did all those things in the second half and got their reward by getting their win.”.

Alan Shearer does not have kind words at half-time for the United squad, labelling the performance “embarrassing”:.

According to recent reports, “There’s not been anything in this performance. I haven’t seen a tackle, a cross, an effort at goal. There is nothing in this performance to be positive about.

“I don’t know where [Carrick] starts because they have been that poor in every department.

“Defensively all over the place, midfield no creativity, and up front no running in behind, no efforts at goal, no holding the ball up. It’s really been embarrassing for them.”.

The last action of the half is another Roma chance, which goes just wide of the top corner.

Boos ring out around Old Trafford as the whistle goes and the players trudge off.

What on earth can Carrick say to his squad to get them to turn this around?

Two minutes of added time begin with Cunha winning a free-kick. Bruno Fernandes passes a short ball forward to Mainoo just outside the area and he has a shot on goal with a neat ball which just dips. Vásquez gets across to collect.

Malen gets another go on goal, finding space down the centre to take a low shot at Lammens, but the keeper is equal to it and gets low to make the save.

Almost something, perhaps a hint of life from United.

Baleba tees up Diallo neatly to make a run into the box but he runs out of room and has to turn the ball back out to Baleba, who first time passes it along the edge of the area. Bruno Fernandes tries to get onto it but it’s an awkward first-time ball and it goes over the bar.

The Roma fans are in loud voice as United again try to progress in the final third.

Sources indicate that malen is booked as Baleba knocks it past him and is hauled down. It’s a decent position to have an attempt on goal, about 35 yards out against a relatively untested keeper.

In a recent development, bruno Fernandes sends it straight into the wall though. A thoroughly underwhelming attempt.

Roma are going forward again, finding space everywhere they look. They pass the ball from left to midfield and out to the right before it comes back to the left, and Mora finds himself on the edge of the area unmarked. A last-ditch challenge from Yoro is the only thing that denies him a shot and United concede a corner.

Mbeumo passes in to Mainoo from the right wing and he makes a run towards the edge of the box but is met by a tight defense. United are not having any luck down the middle and do not look particularly comfortable on the wings.

Baleba wins a free-kick as he is brought down by Cristante. Bruno Fernandes loops a cute ball into the box for Cunha to run onto but Cristante makes another good challenge to get him off the ball.

Roma have hardly put a foot wrong so far.

Balerdi does well to recover the ball as Mbeumo beats him to a header and takes the ball towards the box. The Roma defender makes another very well-timed challenge in the box to deny the striker a chance.

United just aren’t getting forward, they look out of ideas already.

Roma are pressing high on the ball, giving themselves a lot of options to get the ball forward.

Bruno Fernandes is trying to get his team-mates to make runs forward whne they have the ball but Diallo and Mbeumo aren’t quite firing.

Lulli and Soulé by contrast are finding a lot of joy down the right wing. Lulli sends a ball over the box but with too much on it, no one can connect at the back post.

Kobbie Mainoo dances away from two Roma players very tidily, protecting the ball in his own half.

United are trying to get the ball forward but just aren’t finding any space.

Chants of “Jason Wilcox is a w-----” and “Just like the Glazers, Jim Ratcliffe’s a c---” also reverberating. United ownership and executives under constant bombardment.

Cristante tries to send a cross into the box but it takes a looping deflection and is hauled away.

Maguire tries to set Diallo free in the next passage of play but he can’t bring down the long ball sent his way in midfield.

A very good challenge from Wesley to take the ball off Diallo cleanly in the box as the winger made a run in the box.

United showing a bit more fight and trying to put pressure on the third-choice keeper as he plays the ball out.

It has been revealed that baleba has a shot from the edge of the box after a decent passage of play from United around the Roma box. It sails over the bar as he’s just off balance.

Cunha wins the ball and makes a run towards the box. He takes a shot but it is blocked on the edge of the area.

Recent findings suggest that mbeumo goes down off the ball, claiming a foul before Dalot also goes down in the box, looking for a penalty. The official is unmoved.

Fans are throwing objects onto the pitch from the Stretford End.

In the meantime, Rensch has been taken off, replaced by Emanuele Lulli.

United fans are throwing tennis balls on the pitch and chanting “We want Glazers” out – the 20.05 minute protest in a nod to 2005, the year the Americans bought the club. “Sell United and f--- off home,” the Stretford End sings. Mayhem on and off the pitch.

Yellow cards for Bruno Fernandes and Matías Soulé as the two players exchange strong words and a shove.

Rensch went down and Roma players were screaming for the United players to put the ball out of play but they don’t.

According to recent reports, dalot caught in possession and the ball is picked off again. Roma make another run at goal and it’s blocked in the box but United are looking very shaky at the back.

And Donyell Malen makes it two!

He steps up to the spot and cool as you like send Lammens the wrong way to find the back of the net on the keeper’s right.

Malen makes it TWO-NIL ROMA from the spot, after a handball from Heaven in the box 😬 https://t.co/kUeOeQNRES.

It has been revealed that united are in real trouble when they lose the ball. Again they are carved open and Mora takes the ball down the left, sending another looping ball across the field. Soulé tries to find Malen making the run in the box but he can’t quite reach it.

It rebounds at the feet of Soulé and Heaven concedes a penalty for a handball.

Industry observers note that no shots or shots on target for United. One shot on target for Roma and one goal.

But Bruno Fernandes picks the ball up on the right wing from Diallo and fizzes a low ball across the face of goal. Mbeumo can’t quite connect and it is swept away from the feet of Cunha at the far post before he can tap it in.

Industry observers note that this is obviously the last thing United would have wanted. The crowd – previously cheering every ball forward and every challenge – have gone quite quiet.

But just like that, Roma get the breakthrough.

In a recent development, united lose the ball and are carved open. Mora sends a long ball across the field and finds Soulé completely unmarked on the edge of the box. He brings it down, makes a short run and slots it past Lammens low at the near post.

THAT DIDN'T TAKE LONG 😬 United fall behind after just 11 minutes as Roma score through Matías Soulé 🇦🇷 https://t.co/DtIOFJYZ6D.

According to recent reports, mainoo sends a nice pass out to Diallo on the right who sends a ball to Bruno Fernandes on the overlap. His ball into the box is quickly blocked but Mainoo has started very brightly and draws a foul in the next passage of play.

Bruno Fernandes sends a long ball downfield trying to set Mbeumo free but he can’t quite bring it down and control it, and Roma are back on the ball.

Not much in these early exchanges.

Cristante tries to slip a ball through to Malen in the centre of the box but it’s cleared away rapidly.

The Netherlands international picks up the ball again and is swiftly swarmed before he can turn in the box. United staying disciplined so far.

Yoro wins the ball in midfield and United get a bit of possession up the field but a sloppy pass from Dalot gifts it back to Roma and now the visitors are probing the United final third.

But in great news for United, they have reached four minutes without conceding, which is a feat they had not achieved in their last two European games.

Lammens is not taking any chances playing out from the back though, opting for the long ball out every time.

Mainoo tries to lift a ball over the top from midfield for Diallo on the right-hand side, but he doesn’t quite get it right.

According to recent reports, an early goal would definitely boost spirits here. United are enjoying a spell on the ball and that will suffice for now.

And we are underway in Old Trafford!

United need to get off to a steady start here, conceding an early goal could be devastating.

There’s a minute of silence before play in memory of Jesus de ​Miguel who died on Tuesday morning.

As the Champions League anthems plays, fans have released their yellow and green balloons from the stands in protest against the club’s owners.

A mix of boos and cheers from around the ground.

We are five minutes out and both teams are lined up in the tunnel.

One banner in the stands reads “We’ll support you evermore”.

We’re about to see what the players can muster to earn that support.

With kick-off fast approaching, here’s a reminder of the teams taking to the field tonight:.

Man Utd XI (4-2-3-1): Lammens; Dalot, Yoro, Maguire, Heaven; Baleba, Mainoo; Diallo, Cunha, Fernandes; Mbeumo.

Subs: Darlow, Heaton, Amass, De Ligt, Martinez, Mazraoui, Santos, Mount, T Fletcher, Tielemans, Lacey, Zirkzee.

AS Roma XI (3-4–2-1): Vazquez; Mancini, Balerdi, Hermoso; Rensch, Cristante, De Roon, Wesley; Soule, Rodrigo Mora; Malen.

Subs: De Marzi, Koulierakis, N’Dicka, Castro, Molina, Pisilli, Di Nunzio, Lulli, Ghilardi.

Bad timing with injuries means that tonight is the first time that Kobbie Mainoo and Carlos Baleba feature in midfield together.

Baleba was injured when he completed his £70m move from Brighton and Mainoo picked up his muscle injury as his team-mate returned to the substitutes bench.

It will be down to the two young players to stop Roma lacing balls through midfield to Malen and Carrick will need them to click on first time of trying.

Wayne Rooney has decided not to pull any punches tonight when it comes to his former club as he debates the possibility of a upcoming manager arriving at Old Trafford.

It has been revealed that “I’ll tell you Gabby with that group of players, none of the [possible replacement] managers are getting any more out of these players. The biggest job is getting them all out of the football club, that’s the biggest job,” he stated to Gabby Logan.

The United manager has had his turn speaking to Amazon Prime with a very relaxed demeanour, despite the huge pressure sitting on his shoulders.

"It's a SUBSTANTIAL night for us" 🗣️ Carrick gives his thoughts ahead of taking on Roma live on Prime 📺 https://t.co/BHFyKF4fXA.

In a recent development, the former Aston Villa striker has hit the ground running in his first full season with Roma, and has already raced to eight goals and an assist in nine Serie A matches. He notched 14 goals in 18 league matches in the second half of last season while on loan, and has picked up where he left off.

According to recent reports, he’s already scored three in the Champions League, and could be looking eagerly at United’s shaky mentality to add to those numbers. He is the top scorer in Europe’s top five leagues in this calendar year, beating the likes of Lamine Yamal and Harry Kane.

Gasperini’s man-to-man style emphasises his skill in one-on-one situations, where his pace and drive with the ball make him a handful for even the best defenders.

Here is the full list of tonight’s fixtures:.

Matchday 4 is here ⚽️ #UCL https://t.co/tgJlzmaDAh.

Galatasaray are already 2-0 up on Stuttgart, while Sporting have found the breakthrough against Shakhtar Donetsk in the early kick-offs.

Manchester United fans are planning a series of in-stadium demonstrations at Old Trafford tonight in protest at the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s ownership.

Thousands of green and gold balloons – a nod to the club’s original colours as Newton Heath – are set to be released from the Stretford End when the Champions League music plays out ahead of kick-off.

There had been plans to bring a banner into the stadium bearing the words: “No new stadium, we want new owners” but that was blocked, apparently on the grounds of Uefa’s inability to sanction it in time.

The Glazers and Ratcliffe have come under growing attack this season with the club’s regular match going supporters at war with the owners.

A separate fans’ group has also been encouraging fans to join in anti Glazers and Ratcliffe chants in the 21st minute or, more specifically, after 20 minutes and 5 seconds: 20.05 is a nod to 2005, the year the Glazers completed their hostile takeover at Old Trafford.

The main surprise for Roma is in goal, as with first-choice keeper Svilar out already, it has been confirmed that backup keeper Pierluigi Gollini has injured his back today. He has been replaced by Colombian Devis Vásquez in goal.

Roma: Vásquez; Balerdi, Mancini, Hermoso; Rensch, de Roon, Mora, Wesley; Soulé, Cristante; Malen.

Recent findings suggest that we have confirmation, Martínez is on the bench. He is replaced by Ayden Heaven while Bruno Fernandes is still with the captain’s armband in midfield. Kobbie Mainoo gets the nod as he returns from injury, along with Mateus Cunha and Mason Mount.

Your United team for tonight's #UCL clash 👊 https://t.co/TD9F6RjeAB.

Lisandro Martínez has been dropped by Michael Carrick in the wake of his red card madness against Chelsea.

The United manager has opted to pair Ayden Heaven in central defence with Harry Maguire for the Roma game with Martinez dropping to the bench.

The Argentina defender received a second yellow card for planting an elbow in Wesley Fofana’s face in Saturday’s 2-0 defeat at Chelsea when he was also culpable for the first goal.

Martinez has been in dire form this season and was fined and publicly apologised after publicly criticising director of football Jason Wilcox and the Old Trafford board in the wake of the 2-0 defeat by Atletico Madrid.

Kobbie Mainoo returns to midfield after missing the last four games through injury.

Ayden Heaven has just come out to speak with Prime Video, which has led Gabby Logan to assume that means that Lisandro Martínez will not start for Michael Carrick tonight.

Speaking with her, former United legend Wayne Rooney has noted the Argentine has “simply not been good enough” and should not necessarily feature again under Carrick.

When Alan Shearer was asked if he would include Martínez on a team sheet tonight, he did not mince his words, calling him a “liability”.

Ahead of the confirmed line-ups coming out shortly, there are certain players we know we will not be seeing today.

Patrick Dorgu (hamstring), Luke Shaw (unspecified) and Benjamin Sesko (shin) remain sidelined for United, while Marcus Rashford and Amad Diallo will be assessed before the match.

There are no newly introduced concerns for Gasperini after his side’s latest match, the 5-2 win over Udinese, but he remains unable to select Muhammed Bah (ACL), Paulo Dybala, Manu Kone (thigh), Lorenzo Pellegrini (thigh) and first-choice keeper Mile Svilar (stress fracture, foot).

Happy Tuesday and thanks for tuning in to tonight’s coverage of Manchester United against Roma.

It’s matchday four of the Champions League and Michael Carrick’s side host their Serie A opponents having failed to win any of their last nine matches across all competitions. Since their win against Sabah back in September (must feel like years ago to Carrick), they have suffered chastening defeats in Europe to Atlético Madrid and then Cesc Fabregas’s Como. This has been coupled with dismal performances in the Premier League, most recently a 2-0 defeat at the hands of Chelsea, where Lisandro Martínez was sent off for two ridiculous fouls.

Lisandro Martinez is shown a second yellow card following a VAR review 🟥 Watch live on TNT Sports and HBO Max ➡️https://t.co/WPrcA5ZrQ1 https://t.co/VLcAMNdqgZ.

All in all, there is the feeling that Carrick is simply a dead man walking, limping towards the international break after the United hierarchy decided on a stay of execution in their crisis talks earlier this month. If the beleaguered manager has any hope at all of hanging on to his job, he needs convincing results tonight and against Aston Villa on the weekend.

Despite the doom-mongering that circles the club, Carrick maintains that he has buried the hatchet with Bruno Fernandes following his captain’s public criticisms of the club, insisting that “the dressing room is a good place” in his pre-match press conference (more on that to come).

Sources indicate that the visitors on the other hand, managed by Gian Piero Gasperini – who replaced Claudio Ranieri last summer – are certainly having a better time of it. They got off to a slow start in Europe, drawing with Fernebahce in their opening match but coming agonisingly close to stunning Real Madrid on matchday two at home. They went 3-1 up before three late goals snatched victory for Madrid.

Sources indicate that they bounced back with a convincing 4-0 win over Slovan Bratislava and their domestic campaign is off to an incredibly promising start. They are currently unbeaten in Serie A with seven wins and three draws. They sit third and are the highest scoring side, with 28 goals from their 10 games. Free-flowing though their attack is, there a certainly defensive frailties there to exploit as they conceded three in a six-goal thriller against Napoli, as well as two in both matches against Cagliari and Udinese.

Recent findings suggest that it has been 19 years since Carrick was part of a United side that thrashed Roma 7-1 at Old Trafford, with the midfielder scoring two. Tonight he faces that same opponent with his job hanging by a thread and it remains to be seen if his team can produce any semblance of that spark to turn the tide. Feel free to drop us your score predictions in the comments – bragging rights on the line for the winner.

We’ll be bringing you team news, previews from the managers and more ahead of kick-off at 8pm!

Who are the two men running against Gianni Infantino in FIFA president election?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Since replacing Sepp Blatter amid a corruption scandal in 2016, FIFA president Gianni Infantino has solidified his grip on world football’s governing body.

He expanded the men's World Cup to 48 teams, introduced VAR, and has significantly increased development funding for member federations - a move that ensured his unchallenged re-election in 2019 and 2023.

According to recent reports, however, the political landscape has shifted this past year, following a fierce backlash against his aborted strategy to sell stakes in World Cup profits to private investors. In short, Infantino’s uncontested reign is officially over.

In a recent development, two football administrators have formally submitted their candidatures, securing the necessary backing from five member federations. When the 211 member associations vote in Morocco on March 18, 2027, Infantino will face two very different challengers.

Here is a look at the two men attempting to unseat him.

Philippe Diallo represents the most direct threat to Infantino. The 63-year-old took over as president of the French Football Federation (FFF) in 2023, and although a relatively recent arrival into the upper echelons of international football politics, he is a veteran sports administrator.

Backed by UEFA, who have spearheaded the resistance against Infantino, Diallo’s campaign is built upon reform and transparency.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

It has been revealed that diallo has served on the UEFA Executive Committee and balanced domestic reform in France while overseeing a period of success for the national team and women’s game. He recently implemented a major grassroots initiative in France aimed at doubling registered female players to 500,000.

Diallo has lodged a direct attack on Infantino’s 'solitary governance', publicly questioning FIFA’s strategy of seeking private billions when the governing body already holds vast cash reserves.

Recent findings suggest that “My vision is that of open governance,” Diallo recently stated. “It's one where the authorities truly play their role and the president is in charge of vision and strategy but leaves the day-to-day management to the secretary general.”.

Sources indicate that from the Asian Football Confederation (AFC), Kohzo Tashima brings a different background to the election. Tashima, 69, is a former Japanese international who transitioned into coaching youth national teams before climbing the administrative ladder.

Tashima’s experience is embedded in the traditional structures of the sport and served as the president of the Japan Football Association (JFA) from 2016 to 2024. He at the moment holds the title of honorary president. He has also served on both the FIFA Council and the AFC executive committee, earning a reputation as a reliable bureaucrat.

While Diallo focuses on the opacity of Infantino’s reign, Tashima's campaign hinges on a platform of restoring moral authority to FIFA.

According to recent reports, after his candidacy was officially submitted by the JFA, Tashima emphasised the need for a stronger sense of ethics at the top of world football. “We will share with the world the importance of fair play, respect and integrity,” he said. He has vowed to make FIFA a "healthier and more trusted organisation.".

The 2027 election in Morocco could be the most closely contested battle for the definitive seat of world football in generations.
